newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish bonds firm on back of punt strength vs mark.
newsitem.headline: Irish bonds firm on back of punt strength vs mark.

text.p: Irish bonds firmed in late trade on Tuesday, more at the shorter-end than in longer-paper, on the back of punt strength against the mark, dealers said.
"What has been a factor in the background for a month or so has been sterling strength versus the mark which has tended to drive the punt up also versus the mark," Riada's Padraic Garvey said.
"That has had the effect of putting downward pressure on inter-bank rates and has underpinned the short-end. That has been a factor today with the short-end outperforming the longer-paper," he added.
Garvey said other peripheral European markets like Spain and Italy had also seen a steepening of the curve on Tuesday.
"Both Spain and Italy saw a horrific flattening of the curve last Friday as rumours circulated that Germany was set to delay the start of EMU," Garvey said.
"We have seen a recovery in these markets today with the both Spanish peseta and Italian lira stronger against the mark," Garvey said.

By 1600 GMT, the 6.5 percent bond due 2001 was up 17 pence from Monday's close at 102.68 to yield 5.81 percent while the key benchmark eight percent bond due 2006 rose three pence from the close at 110.45 to yield 6.47 percent.
Garvey said that Fed Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan's comments in the second part of his testimony to the House Budget Committeee on Tuesday had little impact on the market.
"He didn't say anything earth-shattering," Garvey said.

Greenspan said it was crucial to keep U.S. inflation down in the short run to help keep the economy purring. He said that low inflation and inflation expectations had been a major reason why the economy had performed so well over the past year.
Looking ahead, Garvey said the market awaited the release of the German unemployment report on Wednesday and U.S. non-farm payrolls data on Friday. --Damien Lynch, Dublin newsroom 353-1-660-3377
